title: Schedule
lede: When this group's books close by themselves, and how often after that. The settlement worker opens a cycle at the moment you state, computes a plan for it, and then moves the schedule on - so the group stops having to remember.
none: Nothing closes this group's books by itself. Every period so far was closed because a member asked for one.

now.cardDescription: The instant below is the group's own, not the moment the worker noticed: a period that falls due while the worker is down is closed late, dated correctly.
now.closes: This group's books close every {everyDays} days.

statement.cardDescription: Setting one replaces whatever the group had: a group has one schedule, so this both starts it and changes it.
statement.everyDaysHint: Between 1 and 366. One is the shortest interval there is; zero would close the books on every pass of the worker, which is why it is refused rather than looped on.
statement.nextDueAtHint: Your browser's time is used, and the instant is what the server stores. It has to be in the future: closing the books now is a plan you ask for, not a schedule that has already fallen due.
statement.intervalNote: A cadence is a number of days rather than a date in the month - "every 30 days" rather than "the 1st" - because a date in the month needs a time zone and a rule for months of different lengths, and this build has decided neither.
